Canary domains are test hostnames that should never return an IP address. Mozilla and Apple run them as tripwires. When an ISP hijacks DNS, these domains return an address instead of failing.
1. Netools sends a lookup for each canary domain to your active DNS resolver.
2. An unmodified resolver returns NXDOMAIN (domain does not exist), confirming clean resolution.
3. If the query returns an IP, CNAME, or SOA record, an intermediary modified the response. The local network is intercepting or redirecting lookups.
4. Netools checks firefox.com and mozilla.org first to confirm internet access before evaluating canaries.
DNS interception lets an operator block sites or record queries before requests leave the local network. Encrypted protocols like DoH or DoT prevent this tampering.
